In moto-x we call this 'monkey-butt' Compression shorts are a great way to avoid this condition.

There are a couple things that could be issues. The first is the easiest, if you wear cotton undies, it's probably them. Cotton is irritating to skin when put into that sort of situation, compression, moisture, vibration... This is why bicycle and compression undies seem to work (it's the synthetic materials, not the padding/compression). As an added bonus, good synthetic undies are WAY cooler/more comfortable in day-to-day wear as well. I converted ~15 years ago and couldn't go back.

The next might simply be endurance. It takes time to build up to longer riding, you simply don't go from a 30 minute commute to a 5+ hour ride without any training between.. just like you don't go from walking to the bathroom to running a marathon without some conditioning/training.

And finally, the seat can/does have a part to play too. Soft foam (most stock seats) do nothing to support. They seem comfortable in the short term, but get a couple hours down the road and the lack of support starts to turn into discomfort. I happen to prefer a very firm saddle foam (just as I prefer a Very firm bed, actually the ground with a thin foam pad is where I get the best rest). Some aftermarket seats are nearly as bad as OEM, some are comfortable for 10 hour days, multiple days in a row, and most are somewhere in between.

Then there's minor things, like staying hydrated (hard to do on a bike), stretching, moving around on the bike, etc... But if you find that 4 hours is your comfort limit, ride out 2~3 hours, take a longer break, then 2~3 hours back. Then start extending that. Ironbutt riders have simply built up to their endurance over time.
